extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: professional scientists and engineers (especially astronomers, telephotography/photography practitioners, archaeologists, and anthropologists)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical methods and performance criteria for early telegraphic photography and planetary photography (how apparatus should operate, what photographic plates should show). Also contains related methodological prescriptions for archaeology, anthropometrics, and radiometric laboratory practice reported in the same journal issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synchronous rotation and spiral scanning (telephotography transmitter)
rubrics_metrics.description: To transmit a picture, the two cylinders are caused to rotate synchronously, at the same time moving from end to end of their traverses; in the course of its spiral path the pinhole H covers successively every point of the focussed image, the illumination of the Se cell being proportional at any moment to the brightness of the spot occupied by the pinhole;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This synchronous rotation and traversing spiral ensures every point of the image is sampled and the selenium cell's illumination (hence resistance) varies in proportion to local brightness, producing the corresponding trace at the receiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving light-relay shutter proportional to transmitter illumination
rubrics_metrics.description: Before reaching the paper the light passes through perforations in two iron plates ... between these is a shutter of aluminium leaf, which is attached to two parallel wires or thin strips forming the bridge C D. When there is no current through C D, the opening is covered by the shutter; when a current traverses the wires, they are depressed by electromagnetic action ... and a quantity of light proportional to the strength of the current is admitted through the perforations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an electromagnet-driven shutter (a 'light-relay') so that intensity of light acting upon the sensitised paper is made proportional to the illumination of the selenium in the transmitter, allowing faithful reproduction of transmitted brightnesses at the receiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation for selenium sluggishness to reproduce half-tones
rubrics_metrics.description: In its response to changes of illumination selenium exhibits a peculiar kind of sluggishness ... Prof. Korn has succeeded in eliminating the effects of the sluggish component by substituting for my box of resistance coils R a second Se cell S2, which is as nearly as possible similar to S1, and which, by means of a second light-relay H2, placed in series with the first, is subjected to similar changes of illumination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place a matched second selenium cell and light-relay in series with the transmitter's selenium so that subpermanent falls in resistance of the transmitter selenium are compensated by equal falls in the second cell; only the immediate (rapid) changes are hence utilised for regulating the transmission current, enabling faithful half-tone transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission resolution / performance metric
rubrics_metrics.description: The parallel lines traced by the point of concentrated light — in this case about 50 to the inch — are easily recognisable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess telephotography performance by the fineness of resolved parallel lines (example given ~50 lines per inch); provide specimen prints to demonstrate resolution over long distances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin planetary observations well before opposition to capture polar-cap evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: From the fact that the observations were begun in March, three months and a half before opposition, it was possible to catch both caps at an interesting phase of their careers — the southern one at its maximum, the northern at its minimum, extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start systematic planetary observations months before opposition to observe seasonal/polar-cap phases and evolution that would be missed by observations only near opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planetary photography standards (detail and measurement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The increased size of disc has enabled the method worked up by Mr. Lampland to be put into even more effective practice ... Plates have been taken ... and the amount of detail they show may be judged from the fact that I have already counted fifty-six canals on my plates ... such delicate markings as the Fens Juventae and the little canals leading to it appear unmistakably in the prints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate methods (e.g., Lampland method, large equatorial) and timing to produce plates with delineatory detail sufficient to count features (canals), photograph delicate markings, and permit positioning of topographic points by measurements from photographs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology for decorative art must be strictly technological
rubrics_metrics.description: The basis of any such system must be strictly technological; it must be a description of what the artist did, of the order in which he did it, and of the effect produced, and all minor elements in the design must be located by reference to the major element on which they are based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a terminology for decorative art that describes the artist's operations (what was done and in what order), the effects produced, and gives locative references of minor elements relative to major elements; build the system gradually with collaboration from interested persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and agreement on anthropological technical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: He urged the importance of the terms used being strictly defined, and also the necessity of some general agreement in their use being obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In anthropological and ethnographic work (e.g., divisions of society, marriage, and descent) strictly define technical terms and seek general agreement among practitioners to ensure comparability and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness in ethnographical surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: It is hoped to extend the survey to all the purely Welsh people, but at present only a limited area has been examined. Still, the results, although purely tentative, are very striking ... the work will be energetically pushed forward, as the population is rapidly changing, and in a comparatively few years it may be too late.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry out ethnographical/ethnographical-survey work promptly while populations retain traditional characteristics; delays risk loss of valuable data due to rapid social change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radium emanation estimation: necessity to fuse solids when using heating method
rubrics_metrics.description: It results from this work that, in the application of the method of heating to the estimation of radium in minerals or other solid substances by the disengagement of the emanation, it is absolutely necessary to fuse the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When estimating radium in solid materials by heating and measuring evolved emanation, ensure samples are fused (molten) so that the whole emanation is evolved and measurements are accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation experiments require uniform temperature control
rubrics_metrics.description: A repetition of the work of H. Le Chatelier, especial care being taken to secure uniformity of temperature. The dissociation pressures are given for six temperatures ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In high-temperature dissociation measurements (e.g., calcium carbonate), take especial care to secure uniformity of temperature across samples and apparatus to obtain reliable dissociation pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical treatment choice affects alloy residue composition (analysis protocol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alloys containing between 57-65 per cent, and 66-76 per cent, of tin treated with hydrochloric acid leave residues richer in nickel, approximating to Ni2Sn3; treatment with nitric acid, on the contrary, gives alloys richer in tin, tending towards NiSn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing nickel-tin (or cobalt-tin) alloys, be aware that choice of acid treatment (HCl vs HNO3) affects which phase remains in residue; select chemical treatment appropriately to reveal desired phases or composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative detection of nickel using molybdate method
rubrics_metrics.description: A new and very sensitive method for the qualitative detection of nickel ... The method is based on the fact that molybdate of nickel is insoluble in presence of an excess of alkaline molybdate, whilst cobalt molybdate is very soluble under the same conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alkaline molybdate precipitation under excess alkaline molybdate to distinguish nickel (insoluble molybdate precipitate) from cobalt (soluble molybdate) as a sensitive qualitative test for nickel.
